issues.description: Inner blocking read loop has no timeout or process-exit backstop
issues.detail: Once O_NONBLOCK is cleared, the inner read loop has no escape if the writer hangs without closing the FIFO. The original code used select.poll and check_process_exited as safety nets; this patch trades an intermittent truncation bug for a potential deadlock. Keep a timeout or process-exit check on the blocking path.

issues.description: fcntl mode flip is permanent, unguarded, and has no error handling
issues.detail: F_GETFL/F_SETFL can fail with OSError, leaving the fd in an inconsistent state. The flip to blocking is also never restored on exit or exception, so any caller that reuses or inherits the fd silently gets blocking semantics. Wrap in try/finally to restore flags and handle fcntl failure explicitly.

issues.description: BlockingIOError handler reduced to silent pass, dropping has_blocking_error semantics
issues.detail: Previously BlockingIOError combined with content meant the file was closed; now the branch is a bare pass and has_blocking_error is gone. After switching to blocking mode this clause is effectively dead. Either delete the except entirely or document why it remains defensive.

issues.description: No regression test for the race condition being fixed
issues.detail: The PR cites an intermittent JSONDecodeError at ~86KB but ships no test that writes a large payload and closes the writer fast. Race fixes without tests get silently re-broken by future refactors. Add a regression test that exercises the truncation path and the new blocking drain.

issues.description: Patch bundles race fix with deletion of a MacOS-specific workaround
issues.detail: The removed block existed because POSIX behavior wasn't reliably observed on MacOS FIFOs. The commit claims POSIX guarantees subsume it but offers no evidence. Either prove MacOS now behaves correctly under the new approach or split the patch and keep the workaround.

issues.description: Two parallel read loops and nested break-out control flow obscure the shape
issues.detail: An outer poll/non-blocking loop and an inner blocking drain loop both append to content and both decide EOF. Extract a small _drain_blocking(fifo_fd) helper and split into wait_for_first_byte then drain_to_eof, with a short docstring naming the two phases. One stream, one termination rule.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The POSIX-blocking-read strategy is the right shape for the FIFO drain problem, but the implementation trades an intermittent truncation race for a potential deadlock: the inner blocking loop has no timeout or process-exit backstop, and the fcntl mode flip is permanent with no error handling or restoration. The patch also silently bundles deletion of a MacOS workaround and drops has_blocking_error semantics without justification, and ships no regression test for a race that already escaped to production. Fix error handling, restore a timeout/process-exit escape on the blocking path, justify or split the MacOS removal, add a regression test, and collapse the two read loops into a single documented two-phase drain.
